title: Harnesses
review: One machine-local reconcile composes folder trust, Codex checkout/lane hook trust, unattended posture and machine hooks (setup enforces bypass even over prior prompting modes; doctor requires actual unattended modes without command-allow fallback; uninstall restores prior modes). Setup, install/refresh, lane preparation and doctor reuse it. Relay home-list changes trigger all registered checkout and lane targets without creating absent harness homes; facet refusals preserve files and teach recovery. Each posture problem names the file it was read from, so doctor and reconcile never label a settings problem with the Desktop config. Setup always includes unattended posture in preview and apply; install and every reconcile caller apply it to every installed harness. There is no permission opt-out. Session posture reads the latest parent Claude hook permission_mode for CLI, Desktop and VS Code; only bypassPermissions passes, and no readable record fails with HARNESS_POSTURE_UNVERIFIED and send any prompt in this chat, then rerun. Hooks cache only the mode and ignore agent_id payloads. Codex CLI and Desktop verify native session identity and the newest turn permission metadata, requiring never plus danger-full-access. Missing, unreadable or out-of-window evidence fails without borrowing saved settings or earlier turns. Cursor CLI keeps its config reader. Codex VS Code and Cursor Desktop warn with HARNESS_POSTURE_CONFIRM_REQUIRED and a setting to confirm; onboarding may proceed after the person confirms it. Unknown surfaces fail. Machine-level saved settings do not prove an active in-session approval mode. Source tests prove late installation, byte-idempotence and backoff; receiving-harness proof remains a release check.
